sources.quote: The investigation into unintended braking in Nissan vehicles, for example, has been open since 2019.
sources.searcher_note: Honda braking story that cites the Nissan probe as open since 2019, against NHTSA's statement that most defect investigations close within 12 months.

sources.searcher_note: Petitioner's release: Nissan admits 1,400+ Rogue AEB reports, no recall, only a 2019 service campaign mailing.

sources.searcher_note: ODI resume opening PE19-010; Date Opened 09/09/2019, population 553,860, 843 complaints, 14 crashes, 5 injuries. PDF; quote taken from extracted text.

sources.quote: The probe covers about 554,000 Rogue small SUVs from the 2017 and 2018 model years.
sources.searcher_note: Earliest wire coverage of the PE19-010 opening; says Nissan could seek a recall.

sources.quote: NHTSA investigated 553,000 Rogues after 800-plus owner reports, 129 confirmed false activations, and 14 accidents that injured five people.
sources.searcher_note: Most recent coverage found; names the Rogue probe but does not say it is still open or give its duration.

notes: Several sources name the Rogue probe and say it was open with no recall (2020, 2022). No source found gives the 7-year / 2,572-day duration or the 234-day median; the closest is Consumer Reports 2022 contrasting 'open since 2019' with NHTSA's 12-month norm. No closure notice or coverage dated after 2026-06-30 found. Related pattern: NHTSA closed a four-year Tesla phantom-braking probe in 2026 (The BRAKE Report, not opened).
